title: With these twelve wines, Juampi Michellini, Matias Riccitelli, Rafael Urreloja and Derek Mossman Knapp illustrate Argentina and Chile’s precocious ability to express the best in any variety
summary: Twelve wines, selected by their maker, four from Zorzal and four from Riccitelli, Undurraga and The Garage Wines Company, were
content:
Twelve wines, selected by their maker, four from Zorzal and four from Riccitelli, Undurraga and The Garage Wines Company, were poured

Of twelve wines tasted, only one was Malbec

Jamie Goode and Lisse Garnett report

Matias Riccitelli

Riccitelli wines command near cultish respect from the initiated, allocations always sell out, and yet the man is genuine, softly spoken and modest. He clearly has a great passion for the wines he is making from Patagonia, as well as in Las Compuertas and Monasterio in Mendoza.

Bastardo, Old Vines From Patagonia 2024

Alcohol 12%, 100% Bastardo aka Trousseau. Grapes sourced from a vineyard in Patagonia, planted in the 70s by some unknown lost lover of this Jura variety. We too love this grape for its dark colour, spice and dried floral notes – the lightness and power it seems to convey and its ultimate silky passage down my gullet. 

Lighter coloured, this is whole bunch fermented, after being foot crushed to avoid carbonic maceration, and then pressed to foudres. Supple and fresg with iron, blood, red cherries, plums and spice. Focused with nice precision: so expressive. 94/100

Semillon, Old Vines From Patagonia 2024 

Alcohol 12%,100% Semillon. An insanely complex, gorgeous wine that will only get better – its honeyed and waxy and fragrant with jasmine, hay, vanilla and candied lemon. Just so pretty, nutty and layered – we were having so much fun that I was unable to contemplate this wine as it deserves, a bottle is an event – I don’t think he makes much and I want more.

Old vines, picked early. Crystalline and light with focused citrus fruit. There’s a bright salinity from some flor aging of some of the wine. Beautiful, expressive, saline and complex. 95/100 (JG)

Pinot Noir, La Carrera 2024 Uco Valley
This is from a new 1700 m site, with some calcareous content in the soils. 30% whole bunch then foudres for 12 months. Ripe but fresh, supple with bright cherry and plum fruit. Very fine and expressive, and juicy and focused. Such presence here. 94/100 (JG)

Chardonnay La Carrera 2024 Uco Valley
From calcareous soils and fermented in foudre. Mineral, fine, fresh and expressive with lovely spiciness. Textural and linear. 95/100 (JG)

Rafael Urrejola, Head Winemaker Undurraga

Modesty again from this highly accomplished winemaker with a voice fit for broadcasting. His family emigrated from the Basque region, from near Gijon, three hundred years ago. They were always connected to wine, but he is the first to turn professional. Cool climate wines became his speciality by default early on in Leyda. He joined what was then a traditional Undurraga in 2007 to initiate Terroir Hunter, a series of radically innovative terroir-specific wines made from carefully chosen and extremely diverse regions. Terroir Hunter has made many experimental wines, driving the need for a sense of place in Chilean viticulture. Urrejola is a champion of Chilean diversity, and he believes multitudinous terroirs, ocean influence and altitude make anything possible in this long, slim country.

Undurraga Terroir Hunter Pinot Noir, Trama 2022

13.5% Alcohol. From a block on limestone in San Antonio Valley, rare in Chile. The climate here is cool and is only five kilometres from the Ocean. Refined, subtle, elegant and fresh, with 25% on stems, gently extracted, indigenous yeast and aged in concrete. Beautifully alive with strawberry, cherry and a fragrant waft of dried aromatic herbs and white pepper. Juicy, sapid and delicious.

Supple and bright with nice concentration, showing sweet raspberry and cherry fruit. Nice compact fruit here with good depth and some crunchy tannins, finishing bright. 94/100 (JG)

Undurraga Terroir Hunter Chardonnay 2023 Limari Valley
13% alcohol. This is a bright, expressive Chardonnay offering orange peel and mandarin notes as well as pear, apricot and spice. But there’s also lovely acidity offsetting this ripe fruit. Lovely. 94/100 (JG)

Undurraga Carmenere Extinto 2022 Cachapoal Valley
14% alcohol. Bright blackcurrant fruit with vibrancy, and some black cherry notes. Focused and rich with some nice spiciness. Intense, salty and mineral. 94/100 (JG)

Undurraga Garnacha Cauquenes 2021 Maule Valley
14.5% alcohol. Garnacha was grafted onto old vines in Cauquenes. Black cherry and blackberry fruit, showing juiciness and a sense of harmony. Lovely. 92/100 (JG)

Juampi Michelini

I was once told Michelini’s are like mushrooms, they spring up everywhere in the wine world – it can be confusing. Juampi aka Juan Pablo Michelini created Zorzal with his brothers Heraldo? And Matias, to create wines that are not market driven but reflect the calcareous mountain terroir from which they came. The Michelini’s have been making groundbreaking wines with little oak and almost no intervention for decades. They drove the vanguard of change in Argentina, harvesting early and looking for cool expression. 

Juampi, “Argentina used to be another country in terms of wine but the 90s style of bold Malbec, hot wine – over oaked, over matured, we didn’t know anything about soils then but we had some certainty about altitude, we knew we wanted freshness, finesse and elegance.” 

Argentina has moved toward terroir specific wines collectively, but the Michelini’s played a star role in that movement.

Zorzal Malbec, Gran Terroir 2024 Uco Valley
13.5% Alcohol, grown on four parcels of limestone and sand, destemmed and fermented in concrete vats its dry – it has texture, tension, Juampi says they have too much, flavour and texture in the grapes so they pair back through low intervention, and ‘infuse’ the grapes. The wine spends one year in old 500 litre barrels.

Ripe but balanced. Fresh and supple with black cherries, plums and spice. Nice black cherry and blackberry fruit here with a grippy edge. This is really good. 94/100 (JG)

Zorzal Chardonnay Terroir Unico 2024 Uco Valley
12.5% alcohol. Lively and powerful with lively citrus and pear fruit as well as some chalky detail. Lovely freshness with good acidity. Fine and crystalline. 93/100 (JG)

Zorzal Eggo Franco Cabernet Franc 2024 Uco Valley
14.5% alcohol. Matured in concrete eggs. Complex, ripe and rich with lovely blackberry fruit. Rich, full and dense with bold ripe fruit and some grainy tannins. Salty, mineral finish. 94/100 (JG)

Zorzal Chardonnay Parcelario 2024 Uco Valley
This is the ‘grand cru’ level. It’s a block of Chardonnay with sme limestone under the soil. Fresh, bright and linear with nice weight and complexity. Such a beautiful wine. 95/100 (JG)

Derek Mossman Knapp, Garage Wines

Derek Knapp has been leading the Maule charge for a long time, and making some excellent wine under the Garage Wines label. Dry farming, old vines, good farming. And cool labelling, too.

Garage Wines Garnacha Carinena Monastrell Parcel Series Sauzal Vineyard Empedrado The Ploughmen 2019 Maule
14.5% alcohol. There’s a savoury, spicy edge to the nose with ripe blackberry and black cherry fruit, as well as some earthy hints. Grippy, fresh and focused with juicy fruit and a bit of tannin, finishing firm and structured. 91/100 (JG)

Garage Wines Single Ferment Old Vine Pale Rosado 2023 Maule
Pale pink in colour. Fresh, supple and bright with nice acidity and juicy cherry and raspberry fruit, with just a bit of grip. Fine, sappy and delicious. 91/100 (JG)

Garage Wines Cabernet Sauvignon Parcel Selection Renacido Vineyard 2021 Maule
Firm but supple at the same time with bright black cherry and blackberry fruit. Juicy with nice focus and some structure, as well as good acidity. No new oak here, and it works very well. 94/100 (JG)

Garage Wines Truquilemu Syrah Lot 84 2019 Maule
Bold, taut and structured with nice black cherry fruit. Grippy, dense and linear with cherries and plums, and some reductive detail. 92/100 (JG)

title: Three wines from a new producer in Oxfordshire (UK): Yew Tree Vineyard
summary: Website: https://yewtreevineyard.com/ Yew Tree is a 5 hectare vineyard in South Oxfordshire, with vines planted in 2015 and 2020 on
content:
Website: https://yewtreevineyard.com/

Yew Tree is a 5 hectare vineyard in South Oxfordshire, with vines planted in 2015 and 2020 on greensand soils. After selling all the grapes for several years (I’ve tried wines from Black Book and Gutter & Stars from their fruit), they now have their own wines, with 2025 the first vintage. They are made and bottled at contract winery Defined Wines. These are priced at £19 direct to consumer.

Yew Tree Ortega 2025 Oxfordshire, England
12.5% alcohol. This is bright, juicy and fruity with a slight grapey edge to the citrus fruit. Juicy and tasty with direct fruit the main theme. It’s very clean with real ripeness as well as good acidity. 88/100

Yew Tree Bacchus 2025 Oxfordshire, England
11.5% alcohol. This is bright and energetic with nice crisp elderflower and citrus fruit, as well as a hint of table grape. Pure and focused with nice concentration, and bracing acidity on the finish. A lovely expression of Bacchus in a dry, tight style, but with plenty of varietal character. 90/100

Yew Tree Rosé 2025 Oxfordshire, England
12% alcohol. This is a blend of Pinot Noir and Pinot Precoce. Appealing mid-pink in colour, this is juicy and fruity with some vibrant raspberry and redcurrant, as well as strawberries and cream. There’s a nice energy to this wine, and it’s very fruit forward and appealing. 89/100

title: Cantina Terlarno and Produttori del Barbaresco: an amazing dinner with two of the world’s great cooperative wineries, tasting back to the 1960s
summary: I was very happy to attend this dinner! Held by the excellent Fine + Rare at Wiltons, the evening featured
content:
I was very happy to attend this dinner! Held by the excellent Fine + Rare at Wiltons, the evening featured 25 wines with both producers going back to the 1960s. Are these the best cooperatives in the world? On this showing, it’s hard to argue against.

Cantina Terlano

Website: https://www.cantina-terlano.com/en/

Klaus Gasser introduced Cantina Terlano, who are based in the Alto Adige. He’s the director of marketing and sales there. The winery was founded in 1893 at the time of the Austro-Hungarian empire, and this region passed to Italy at the end of the first war. ‘Tyrol is cut in two,’ says Gasser. ‘In the daytime we are Germans and in the nighttime we are Italians.’

The region is close to Graubunden in Switzerland, but now has a very strong Italian influence.

Terlano has its own appellation (DOC Alto Adige Terlano), and the Cantina has a monopoly situation, with the 200 or so families growing grapes here all supplying the cooperative. There is no ‘village level’ quality here. On the flats, there are many fantastic apple farmers. Then on the hills leading to the mountains, the vineyards are all top notch. The grapes are grown from altitudes of 230-900 m, but the sweet spot is 550-650 m, and the famed Vorberg is 400-900 m.

The average holding here is 1.2 hectares (there are 1500 parcels), and they are expensive (around €1 m/hectare). They did a classification of the vineyards 25 years ago, and if you have the grand cru holdings, you get a lot of money for your grapes. Average yields are a decent 49 hl/ha. ‘We keep the money in the region,’ says Gasser, ‘and this keeps the families in the region.’

When the winery was founded in 1893 the grapes in the region were Pinot Bianco and Chardonnay (although this was originally called yellow Pinot Bianco, and it wasn’t identified as Chardonnay until 1984). Then Sauvignon Blanc came to the region in 1910.

Cantina Terlano Vorberg Riserva 2023 Alto Adige Terlano, Italy
Pinot Bianco, fermented and aged in large oak casks and cement tanks. 18 months on lees. Beautiful freshness and tension with delicate fine herbal notes and some minerals. Expressive and fine with a tapering finish. 93/100

Cantina Terlano Vorberg Riserva 2019 Alto Adige Terlano, Italy
There’s a bit of richness here with pear and white peach, as well as nice tension, and some fine spices. Slight salinity. This has focus and delicacy, with a slight green hint that works well. 95/100

Cantina Terlano Vorberg Riserva 1966 Alto Adige Terlano, Italy
Golden colour, with nuts, honey and spice. Harmonious with lovely precision still, as well as nutty, appley depth. Finishes broad and salty. 95/100

Cantina Terlano Pinot Bianco Rarity 2013 Alto Adige Terlano, Italy
This comes from 50 year old vines at 570 m in Vorburg and is aged in 2500 litre casks for one year, then minimum 10 years on lees in stainless steel. They have vintages back to 1979 still on lees. This was bottles in August 2025. Pure, textural and precise with lovely tension, showing a saline twist to the bold citrus and pear fruit with a hint of apple. Very fine. 95/100

Cantina Terlano Pinot Bianco Rarity 2010 Alto Adige Terlano, Italy
This was bottled after 11 years on lees, but they have kept some back that was bottled after 15 years on lees. Subtle honeyed notes with nice texture and some crystalline citrus fruit, showing firm, spicy detail, as well as a slight saltiness. Powerful and bold with great concentration of fruit. 95/100

Cantina Terlano Pinot Bianco Rarity 2005 Alto Adige Terlano, Italy
Some honeyed, oxidative notes. Bold and expansive with some green pepper and tinned pea. Quite rich, but with some tension, and nice acidity. 94/100

Cantina Terlano Nova Domus Terlaner Riserva 2023 Alto Adige Terlano, Italy
This is a field blend of 60% Pinot Bianco, 30% Chardonnay and 10% Sauvignon Blanc. 18 months in 3000 litre casks. Complex and layered with bold pear and peach fruit with some pithy notes. Slightly salty with nice tension, and some richer peachy notes. 94/100

Cantina Terlano Nova Domus Terlaner Riserva 2013 Alto Adige Terlano, Italy
This is 65% Pinot Bianco, 30% Chardonnay and 5% Sauvignon Blanc. Subtle toast, mineral and spice on the nose. Really lovely tension with bright apple, pear and white peach fruit. Still youthful and fresh with real intensity and balance. 95/100

Cantina Terlano Primo Grand Cuvée 2023 Alto Adige Terlano, Italy
Lovely focus, with spice and a hint of toast on the nose. Lemon and lime fruit showing nice depth on the palate with some slight saltiness. Very sophisticated, with beautiful depth and intensity. Still quite primary. 94/100

Cantina Terlano Primo Grand Cuvée 2016 Alto Adige Terlano, Italy
Some honey and spice on the nose. Textured with fine spices alongside pear and peach fruit on the palate, as well as a twist of lime brightness. Very fine with lovely weight. 95/100

Cantina Terlano 1983 Alto Adige Terlano, Italy
Pinot Bianco and a bit of Silvaner. 8 months in large oak. Complex with fine spices and notes of wax and honey. Lovely crystalline citrus fruit. Saline and slightly smoky with some incense notes. Beautiful. 96/100

Cantina Terlano Rarity 1991 Alto Adige Terlano, Italy
60% Pinot Bianco, 30% Chardonnay, 10% Sauvignon Blanc This spent one year in large oak then 24 years on lees in stainless steel. Delicate, pristine and focused. Fresh and textured with bold citrus fruit showing real intensity and purity. A beautiful, layered wine. 96/100

Produttori del Barbaresco

Website: https://www.produttoridelbarbaresco.com/en/

Managing director Luca Cravanzola introduced Produttori del Barbaresco. This is a very small cooperative working solely with Nebbiolo. They have Langhe Nebbiolo, Barbaresco, and then nine top crus of Barbaresco, which they first started making in 1967.

Fifty-three farmers belong to the cooperative, and altogether they farm just 120 hectares, which makes this a very small cooperative. Barbaresco is small, and there are just 300 hectares in total.

This cantina sociale dates back to 1894, but closed with fascism in the 1920s. After this Barbaresco had lots of troubles and most of the Nebbiolo was sold to wine merchants with quite a bit ending up in Barolo. The lure of the factories in Torino led people away from the land. Produttori as we know it began in 1958.

Produttori del Barbaresco Barbaresco 1998 Piemonte, Italy
This was a good vintage, but they didn’t bottle the single vineyards this year. Full in colour. Textured and fine with a hint of Portiness. Lovely weight and texture, showing richness and a warm spicy dimension. Bold with amazing depth and richness. This is beautiful in a rich, ripe style. 95/100

Produttori del Barbaresco Barbaresco 1983 Piemonte, Italy
Another year with no single crus. Faded colour, browning. This has beautiful aromas of spice and madeira, with orange peel, wax and old furniture. Lovely depth with fine spicy detail. It’s really mature, but still offers a lot of joy. 94/100

Produttori del Barbaresco Barbaresco 1982 Piemonte, Italy
A great year, and a truly great wine. Still vibrant in colour with a slightly bricking rim showing its age. This has a lovely savoury, spicy edge with sweet red cherries and plums as well as a hint of mint. Really amazing texture and finesse. So elegant, drinking beautifully with lovely finesse. Remarkable. 98/100

Produttori del Barbaresco Barbaresco 1975 Piemonte, Italy
Quite deep in colour. Notes of tar, spice, resin and dried herbs. Lovely density with a savoury, spicy edge to the raspberry and cherry fruit. Quite firm and savoury with nice density. Earthy. Interesting. 94/100

Produttori del Barbaresco Barbaresco 1973 Piemonte, Italy
Warm and spicy with nice texture and real elegant. Juicy with fine spices. So supple and elegant with real finesse. Fine and herby with some cherry fruit and a touch of iron. Tapering, expressive and really beautiful. 97/100

Produttori del Barbaresco Barbaresco 1967 Piemonte, Italy
This still has some colour with just a bit of bricking at the rim. Refined and finely spiced with some maturity, but also real elegance and still has some fruit. Fine-grained and beautifully expressive with subtle salinity. Just beautiful. 96/100

Produttori del Barbaresco Barbaresco Rabajá 2020 Piemonte, Italy
The crus are made in top vintages, and they make all 9 or none. Such finesse and purity here. Raspberry and cherry fruit with good texture and weight. Such elegance to this wine, with purity to the fruit and a silky mid-palate. Beautifully layered. 96/100

Produttori del Barbaresco Barbaresco Rabajá 2011 Piemonte, Italy
Still dark in colour, this shows lovely detail. It’s savoury, tarry and slightly spicy with black cherries and blackberries, and a bit of tannic grip. Nice intensity, showing a savoury edge. 94/100

Produttori del Barbaresco Barbaresco Riserva Montestefano 2016 Piemonte, Italy
This is considered to be the Barolo from Barbaresco, with more tannin than most. Nice intensity. Classic style with some fine spicy detail. Lovely density, showing fine spices, black cherry and good grip and intensity. Beautiful stuff. 95/100

Produttori del Barbaresco Barbaresco Riserva Montestefano 2014 Piemonte, Italy
Concentrated and focused with black cherry and blackberry fruit. Amazing precision here with silky cherries, berries and lovely spicy intensity. Refined and dense at the same time. 96/100

Produttori del Barbaresco Barbaresco Pora Riserva 1988 Piemonte, Italy
This is the closest of the 9 crus to the river, and there’s some sand and limestone in the soils. Savoury, spicy and taut. Mineral with notes of wax and woodsmoke. Dense and spicy. This is quite brisk but the tannins are silky. 93/100


Produttori del Barbaresco Barbaresco Pora Riserva 1982 Piemonte, Italy
Complex, taut and savoury. Bold with a touch of iodine and spice. Concentrated and firm with nice density and some savoury structure. Still quite grippy with lovely focus to the citrus and orange peel. Cherry and spice notes too. 96/100

Produttori del Barbaresco Barbaresco Ovelli 1979 Piemonte, Italy
Spicy, savoury and a bit earthy. Nice spicy detail with some freshness. Savoury and grainy with nice detail. Earthy and intense. 93/100

title: The 2025 wines from Pascal Jolivet in Sancerre
summary: Website: https://pascaljolivet.com/en/ These are the 2025 releases from leading Sancerre-based producer Pascal Jolivet. This was a good vintage, but not
content:
Website: https://pascaljolivet.com/en/

These are the 2025 releases from leading Sancerre-based producer Pascal Jolivet. This was a good vintage, but not a simple one. Winter rainfall was good, but then it was dry and warm from the outset. Early budbreak was followed by the driest May and June in 15 years. Then there was a heatwave in August, and despite some rain on 20 August, sugar accumulation was rapid and it was a late August and early September vintage. The grapes were in perfect condition, but this was a year for rich, ripe wines that searched a bit for definition and typicity.

I really liked these wines, though. Jolivet have done a really good job, and while they aren’t the most typical examples of their place, they are delicious.

Pascal Jolivet Edition Sauvignon Blanc 2025 Coteaux de Giennois, Loire, France
12.5% alcohol. Jolivet have 20 hectares in this appellation, in Saint-Père, a special part. Limestone/flint soils. Delicate but full nose of apple, pear and citrus, with a hint of elderflower. The palate is quite full, concentrated and rounded with a slight saltiness to the bold fruit. Really weighty, despite the low alcohol, finishing fresh with a slight green hint. This is really textural. 93/100

Pascal Jolivet Blanc Fumé 2025 Loire, France
13.5% alcohol. This is bright and linear with nice fennel and herb notes as well as boldly textured pear and citrus fruit, with a hint of apple. This has great concentration with real refinement, showing rounded, textured fruit with some warmth and depth. There’s a crystalline, crushed rock minerality here. The serious mineral end of the wine is slightly masked by the rich fruit now, but it’s there. 93/100

Pascal Jolivet Sancerre 2025 Loire, France
13.5% alcohol. Beautiful aromatics with ripe pear and peach as well as some elderflower. The palate is beautifully nuanced, showing crystalline citrus fruit and some melon and pear richness, with very subtle green characters. There’s a grapefruit frill on the finish. This is really expressive and shows the riper side of Sancerre really well. Very fine. Lovely stuff. 94/100

Pascal Jolivet Sauvage Sancerre 2025 Loire, France
14% alcohol. This is a parcel selection from 2 hectares of limestone terroirs located in the villages of Champtin and Bué-en-Sancerre. Organic. Wild ferment then ageing on lees for 12 months in stainless steel. This is rich and textural with lovely depth to the saline-laced pear and melon fruit, with some crystalline citrus. Such a plump, rich, textural expression of Sancerre, with the limestone showing on the finish in terms of the acid line, but it’s almost hidden by the weight of rich fruit, a function of the vintage. Almost Cotat-like in style, this is rich, but should age effortlessly with that mineral extract. I’d love to see this again in a decade. 95/100

Pascal Jolivet Les Caillottes Sancerre 2025 Loire, France
13% alcohol. Organically farmed. This is fresh, detailed and quite delicious, with ripe pear and citrus fruit and a nicely textured mid-palate, finishing broad but with a finely spiced flourish. It’s a bit chalky, too. Very stylish with a lot of dimensions, and showing the richness of the year. 94/100

Pascal Jolivet Clos du Roy Sancerre 2025 Loire, France
15% alcohol. Jolivet have 0.79 hectares of this 18 hectare clos, which is in the village of Crézancy-en-Sancerre. Stainless steel. This is textured and rich with a lovely rounded mouthfeel, and salty minerality supporting the ripe pear and peach fruit. There’s some warmth and texture from the alcohol, but a lot of concentration, and I expect this should age well, even if it isn’t a typical Sancerre. Rich, layered and saline. 94/100

title: Quinta da Vinha dos Padres: remarkable wines from Portugal’s Alentejo
summary: These three wines, made by Susana Esteban, are really impressive. They come from Serra de São Mamede, in the Portalegre
content:
These three wines, made by Susana Esteban, are really impressive. They come from Serra de São Mamede, in the Portalegre region of Alentejo, from high altitude (546-562 m). The old vineyards (100 years+) are planted as a field blend, with mixed varieties. Winemaking is in talhas (clay vessels) of 300-2000 litres.

Quinta da Vinha dos Padres Vila Maria Branco 2022 Portalegre, Alentejo, Portugal
Golden colour. Wonderful aromatics of apple, peach and pear with lovely spicy notes. Textured and full with a saline twist and some nice grainy structure. Notes of aniseed, dried herbs, finishing fresh. This is really beautiful and harmonious, with so many dimensions to it. 95/100

Quinta da Vinha dos Padres Vila Maria Tinto 2022 Portalegre, Alentejo, Portugal
This is a field blend red. One year in talha. Beautiful restraint and elegance with fine-grained red cherry and berry fruits, with nice dry tannins supporting the elegant fruit. Notes of clay and minerals, too. There’s a core of sweet fruit that is beautifully balanced by some grip and savoury detail. 94/100

Quinta da Vinha dos Padres Vila Maria Branco 2023 Portalegre, Alentejo, Portugal
Highly aromatic with dried herbs, mint, aniseed, clay and chalk. The palate is bold and richly textured with a nice pear, apple, peach fruitiness and then some grapey richness. And it’s deliciously stony and mineral. Shows so many layers of flavour. Ripe and rich but with excellent balance. 95/100

title: Australia’s Clare Valley: a mini-study in six wines
summary: The Clare Valley is an interesting region in South Australia that’s made its reputation on Riesling and Cabernet Sauvignon, as
content:
The Clare Valley is an interesting region in South Australia that’s made its reputation on Riesling and Cabernet Sauvignon, as well as turning out very smart Shiraz. I tried through these six wines.

Pauletts Polish Hill River Riesling 2025 Clare Valley, Australia
11% alcohol. Slate soils. This is juicy and chalky with a strong lemony character and good acidity. It’s quite lean and focused but not austere, and there are some really nice floral notes. Has a compact character, a subtle oiliness and a tight finish. Classic, with good intensity, and a long future ahead of it. 93/100

Pikes Traditionale Riesling 2025 Clare Valley, Australia
11% alcohol. Brisk and limey, and quite vivid with high acidity. Dry and linear. This is really juicy and focused with nice energy and transparency. There’s a slight chalkiness, too. 93/100

Grosset Polish Hill Riesling 2025 Clare Valley, Australia
12.3% alcohol. Taut, focused nose of lemon and lime with some floral hints. Honeysuckle and maybe even some jasmine. In the mouth this has wet stone minerality with delicate citrus fruit, showing lovely poise and balance, and a touch of chalkiness. 94/100

Jim Barry The Florita Riesling 2024 Clare Valley, Australia
12% alcohol. This is complex and limey, with lovely texture. There’s some breadth to the fruit as well as spicy grapefruit framing, a touch of margarita, and nice tension and balance. Such purity here: this blends concentration with refinement. 94/100

Mount Horrocks Shiraz Alexander Vineyard 2022 Clare Valley, Australia
On opening this has a peppery edge and some muted, slightly reductive berry fruit aromas. Supple herb-laced cherry and plum fruit on the palate. Midweight and slighty angular with some sour acid on the finish. Brisk and very Australian in style. Tastes a bit too acidified? But otherwise really nice. 90/100

Wakefield St Andrews Cabernet Sauvignon 2018 Clare Valley, Australia
[Wakefield is the name used by Taylors for export markets.] Lovely aromatics here with sweet herb-laden blackcurrant fruit, with some strawberry and mint in the mix. Richly textured with a lovely smoothness to the mid-palate, showing sweet blackcurrant and cherry fruit and fine-grained earthy, leafy complexity. Approachable but also has seriousness. 94/100

title: Profetas e dos Villões: António Maçanita and his remarkable wines from Porto Santo and Madeira
summary: Website: https://www.antoniomacanita.com/en António Maçanita is a well known Portuguese winemaker, doing good things in the Alentejo, Douro and the Açores.
content:
Website: https://www.antoniomacanita.com/en

António Maçanita is a well known Portuguese winemaker, doing good things in the Alentejo, Douro and the Açores. But some of his most remarkable wines come from a small island next to Madeira, Porto Santo.

Here he has established a Profetas e dos Villões, in conjunction with a friend Nuno Faria, who runs a restaurant on Madeira. Maçanita calls it his ‘Covid project’.

The name translates as prophets and villains: the Madierans refer to Porto Santo folk as prophets, and they in turn refer to Madeirans as villains. Faria spent his childhood holidays on Porto Santo, and he told Maçanita about the vineyards here.

Porto Santo has a very different climate to Madeira. Madeira is mountainous, and gets a lot of rainfall, hence it is lush and green. Porto Santo is flat and only gets 380 mm of rain a year, which makes it arid. The soils are different to Madeira, too: calcareous sandstones.

The first wines were made in Madeira, but since 2022 there is a winery on Porto Santo.

In addition to the Profetas (Porto Santo wines) he’s also added some Madeiran wines to the project (Villões). The wines are mainly labelled DOP Madeirense, but the nicknames are used to distinguish them. Since some of the wines were made in the new winery on the island, they can be labelled DO Porto Santo

António Maçanita Profetas e dos Villões Caracol Fazendas Areia 2021 Porto Santo, Portugal
Lovely density with notes of orange peel and lime. Stony and vivid with keen acidity, nice depth and subtle waxy detail. Intriguing. 94/100

António Maçanita Profetas e dos Villões Caracol Fazendas Areia 2023 Porto Santo, Portugal
Very taut, but still has some depth. Lemons, wax and minerals with crystalline citrus and some keen acidity. So fine. 95/100

António Maçanita Profetas e dos Villões Caracol dos Profetas Uvas Passas 2022 Porto Santo, Portugal
This is passito style and spends 3 years in cask. Nuts, honey and lime on the nose. The palate is powerful and lively with a hint of raisin, and some lime and marmalade. Bold, intense, yet balanced, with a salty finish. Such a wine. 96/100

António Maçanita Profetas e dos Villões Listrão dos Profetas 2021 Porto Santo, Portugal
80 year old vines. Waxy, stony and bright, this is vivid with nice energy. Taut and focused with limey fruit. Very expressive. 95/100

António Maçanita Profetas e dos Villões Sercial Los Villões 2023 Madeira, Portugal
Concentrated and linear with nice texture to the powerful citrus fruit. Crystalline with nice lemony acidity. Bold. 94/100

António Maçanita Profetas e dos Villões Crosta Calcária 2023 Porto Santo, Portugal
This is from the centre of the island. Very fine, linear and refined with crystalline citrus fruit on the nose. The palate is smoky, spicy and mineral, and quite refined with explosive energy. Lemony, intense and thrilling. 97/100

António Maçanita Profetas e dos Villões Tinta Negra dos Villões 2022 Madeira, Portugal
Chalky edge to the nose. Supple, juicy and vivid with nice red cherry fruit. Great focus and energy with real refinement. Lovely balance. 94/100

Older notes:

António Maçanita Profetas e dos Villões Listrāo does Profetas 2021 Porto Santo, Portugal
Very linear, fine and pure. Bright and saline with high acidity. Concentrated, showing pure lime fruit with a hint of pear. 96/100

António Maçanita Profetas e dos Villões Caracol dos Profetas 2021 Porto Santo, Portugal
Smoky, spicy, mineral nose with very fine chalky citrus fruit on the palate. Mineral and stony with lovely saline citrus character. 95/100

António Maçanita Profetas e dos Villões Caracol Fazendas Areia 2021 Porto Santo, Portugal
Bright, concentrated and mineral with lovely precision to the fine citrus fruit. Lively with lovely intensity. 96/100

António Maçanita Profetas e dos Villões Tinta Negra dos Villões 2021 Madeira, Portugal
Supple and fresh with fine red cherries and raspberries on the nose. The palate is fine and supple with juicy cherries and raspberries showing amazing precision. Fine green hints, too. 95/100

António Macanita Caracol dol Prefetas 2021 Porto Santo, Portugal
Caracol is the grape variety here, grown on Porto Santo island then shipped to next door Madeira for vinification. Clay/limestone soils at 50 m altitude, 40-80 year old vines trained low because of winds, fermented in stainless steel. Taut and saline with lovely precision, showing some mineral notes. Tight citrus fruit on the palate with a touch of apple, showing fine spiciness and good acidity. Some salinity too. Amazing tension here. 95/100

content:
Website: https://langhamwine.co.uk/product/perpetual-cuvee/

This is the second release of the much-heralded Perpetual cuvée from leading English sparkling wine producer Langham. It’s a very serious wine.

Langham Perpetual Chardonnay Second Edition Brut Nature NV Dorset, England
12% alcohol. This contains 2017, 18, 19 and 20, and was disgorged in July 2025. Wonderful aromatics of honey, almonds, baked bread and ripe lemon, pear and peach fruit. The palate is concentrated and broad with lively lemony fruit supplemented with peach and toast. Such a lovely, expanding finish. Expansive, complex and very long. Quite beautiful. 97/100 (£110 direct from Langham, 1 bottle limit)

title: Usonia, a really innovative wine project from New York’s Finger Lakes
summary: Website: https://www.usoniawine.com/ While I was in the region in June I ran into a new producer, Usonia, who are doing
content:
Website: https://www.usoniawine.com/

While I was in the region in June I ran into a new producer, Usonia, who are doing things a bit differently.

Julia and Alex Alvarez-Perez have worked in Austria’s Burgenland, and also Australia’s Adelaide Hills. In the Finger Lakes, they are trying to find a way forward for this region that tells its own story.

They are working with hybrids but making interesting wines (normally hybrids aren’t taken seriously), as well as doing a bit with vinifera. They officially launched in 2020 and have their own 4.5 acre vineyard on the west side of Cayuga Lake, planted with Cabernet Franc and Riesling, the two star vinifera varieties in the region. But in 2022 they started getting into hybrids. Finger Lakes will always have quite a lot of hybrids because of the climate: away from the protective effect of large bodies of water, winters are just too cold for vinifera. Now people are working more creatively with them, which is good to see.

Usonia Cayuga White 2024 Finger Lakes, New York
Hand picked, direct pressed and fermented and matured in fibreglass. Supple, fruity and stony, with juicy fruit. Quite delicate and pure. 90/100

Usonia Soon Different 2025 Finger Lakes, New York
This beautiful rosé is made from organically farmed Regent, Aravel and Arabella. Juicy and lively with strawberry and redcurrant. Nice brightness here with some herby detail. Lovely. 91/100

Usonia Member When 2024 Finger Lakes, New York
This is Geneva White No 2 (in plastic tank on skins) and Verdelet (in 500 litre barrel). Organic. Nice weight here with some structure and stony spicy detail. Grainy, pure and showing some complexity with nice tannins. This is lovely. 91/100

Usonia Good Spirit 2021 Finger Lakes, New York
Cofermented Baco Noir, Chaloire and Traminette. Juicy and fruity with berry fruits and nice grip. Has good fruit purity. This is delicious, fresh and pure. 92/100

Usonia Pompliano Purple 2024 Finger Lakes, New York
Biodynamically farmed Sabrevois. Full coloured. Fresh and stony with a bit of wood spice. Lovely pure fruit, with some freshness and brightness. Direct and pure. 91/100

Usonia Pompliano Pink 2025 Finger Lakes, New York
This is Steuben, biodynamically farmed. Foot trodden and left overnight then transferred to a neutral barrel. No sulfite additjons. Supple fresh and bright with pear, cherry and redcurrant. Fine-grained with lovely texture and a nice acid line. 93/100

Usonia New Skins Riesling 2023 Finger Lakes, New York
This is from the home vineyard and one third is carbonic maceration for a week. Full malolactic. Juicy, fresh and fine with nice delicate citrus fruit, a hint of mandarin and melon, and nice weight. 91/100

Usonia Riesling Standing Stone Farms 2023 Finger Lakes, New York
Direct press, 80% to stainless, 20% to neutral barrel. Juicy and textural with nice pear and spice as well as green apple. Lovely weight and balance, showing real finesse. Has depth. 92/100

title: Herrenhof Lamprecht: impressive wines from volcanic Styria, with a particular focus on Furmint and field blends
summary: Website: https://www.herrenhof.net/ Back in the day, Herrenhof Lamprecht, now a wine estate in Vulkanland Steiermark (Austria) was a monastery. There’s
content:
Website: https://www.herrenhof.net/

Back in the day, Herrenhof Lamprecht, now a wine estate in Vulkanland Steiermark (Austria) was a monastery. There’s a lot of history here, but for the current phase wine production started in 2005, just over 20 years ago. Now there are 11 hectares of vines here, including 3 hectares of their speciality, Furmint.

I tasted these wines with Gottfried Lamprecht. He makes all the wines in 600 litre barrels, and half the oak for these comes from his own forest. The wines are naturally made, but there are some sulfur dioxide additions before bottling.

These wines are really impressive.

Herrenhof Lamprecht Cremant de Herrenhof 2021 Vulkanland Steiermark, Austria
This is Furmint. Bright and linear with nice energy. Great acidity. Pure and transparent. 90/100

Herrenhof Lamprecht Furmint von Sandstein 2023 Vulkanland Steiermark, Austria
Stony and linear with vivid fruit. Nice acidity here. Fresh with good texture and purity. 91/100

Herrenhof Lamprecht Furmint von Sandstein 2024 Vulkanland Steiermark, Austria
Textured with nice depth to the pear and citrus fruit, with a mineral twist. Nice layers of flavour here with great texture. 93/100

Herrenhof Lamprecht Sand + Kalk 2024 Vulkanland Steiermark, Austria
This is Pinot Blanc. Linear, showing finesse to the citrus and pear fruit with a touch of peach. Great precision and finesse with lovely weight. 94/100

Herrenhof Lamprecht Riesling Pax Dei 2023 Vulkanland Steiermark, Austria
Normally the Riesling goes into the field blend, but in good years this is bottled separately. From sandstone soils. Lively and pure with textured lemony fruit. Textured with some stony, mineral notes and real finesse. 94/100

Herrenhof Lamprecht Buchterberg Gemischter Satz Weiss 2023 Vulkanland Steiermark, Austria
This is a field blend (with some old pre-phylloxera varieties in the mix), something that used to be common in Styria. Two years in oak. Complex and layered with nice concentration, showing lovely density, bold crystalline citrus notes and some salinity. Concentrated and really fine. 95/100

Herrenhof Lamprecht Buchterberg Gemischter Satz Weiss 2021 Vulkanland Steiermark, Austria
Salty and lemony; pure and fine. Has nice texture and presence and tastes really harmonious. Lovely stuff. 95/100

Herrenhof Lamprecht Schrammelberg Alsteirischer Mischatz 2023 Vulkanland Steiermark, Austria
They buy these grapes, which come from 90 year old vines. Ungrafted field blend. Concentrated, mineral and fine with pear and citrus fruit. Very fine and mineral with good tension. 95/100

Herrenhof Lamprecht Sand & Kalk ‘r’ 2022 Vulkanland Steiermark, Austria
This is Pinot Gris, with two years in oak. Supple and bright with mandarin and citrus, as well as spice and pear. Layered with lovely acid line, nice salinity and a hint of apple. 94/100

Herrenhof Lamprecht Buchterberg Rosé 2024 Vulkanland Steiermark, Austria
Field blend of red grape varieties. Supple and fine, and slightly saline. Crystalline with red cherry and pear fruit, as well as some pear and apple. So lovely. 93/100

Herrenhof Lamprecht Pinot Noir Rosé 2022 Vulkanland Steiermark, Austria
Deep orange/red in colour. Leafy edge to the bright cherry and pear fruit with nice tannins and some spiciness. Lovely texture to this wine. 93/100

Herrenhof Lamprecht Buchterberg Rot 2022 Vulkanland Steiermark, Austria
A field blend, 30 days on skins. Supple and bright with lively red cherry fruity spice and some pepper. Nice weight and intensity with lovely direct fruit. Very stylish and textural. 94/100

Herrenhof Lamprecht Buchterberg Rot 2023 Vulkanland Steiermark, Austria
Floral and fresh with nice cherry and raspberry fruit. Bright with great energy. Juicy, brisk and chalky and mineral, with real focus and intensity, but also elegance. 94/100
